q: Walk me through your background in 60 seconds.
a: Lead with the business outcome you're known for, then your current scope (team, scale, reliability), two earlier roles that show breadth, one cost or growth result, and one line on why this company.

q: Why are you leaving your current role?
a: Frame it as moving toward something: more scope, a bigger function, a domain you want. Never criticize your current employer.
If a range is posted and it works: say so and that you're flexible on the full package. If not: give your floor and ask whether there is flexibility or a higher level.
tip: Know your floor before the call.

q: What would you do in your first 90 days?
a: Days 1-30 listen and baseline metrics, risks, budget and vendors. Days 31-60 stabilize and take first wins. Days 61-90 set the roadmap, org design and a few metrics you report monthly.

q: Tell me about a time you failed.
a: Pick a real miss you owned. Situation, what you did wrong, what you changed, and the measurable result afterwards.

q: How do you influence people who don't report to you?
a: A specific initiative: who resisted, what they cared about, how you reframed it in their terms, and the outcome.

q: Walk me through how you handle a major incident.
a: Severity and escalation, a single incident lead, customer communication, restore first then root cause, blameless review with tracked actions.
tip: Give one real incident and the time to restore.

q: What if they ask about something you haven't done?
a: Say so plainly, explain how you'd approach it, and bridge to the closest thing you have done.
